paper_title: First Results from the Taiwan Axion Search Experiment with Haloscope at 19.6 $μ$eV
coupling_convention: |g_agamma| in GeV^-1 (y-axis plotted in units of 10^-14 GeV^-1; multiplier applied)
notes: TASEH haloscope first results at 4.70750-4.79815 GHz (19.4687-19.8436 ueV). 95% C.L. limits on |g_agamma| range from 5.3e-14 to 8.9e-14 GeV^-1 with average 8.2e-14 GeV^-1; the average value is used as a flat band over the stated mass range since the full frequency-dependent limit curve is only shown graphically (Fig. 2), not tabulated. Assumes axions constitute 100% of local DM with rho = 0.45 GeV/cm^3, standard Maxwellian line shape with <v^2> = (270 km/s)^2. Two narrow frequency ranges (4.71017-4.71019 GHz and 4.74730-4.74738 GHz) are excluded from limits due to non-axion interference signals. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.9, 44)) | Vision: TASEH first results (arXiv:2205.05574). Baseline limit ~8.2e-14 GeV^-1 (11x KSVZ), with downward dips to ~5.2-7.5e-14 at candidate frequencies where additional data was collected.
